purpose: Authoritative-vendor manufacturing integration delta. Adds Rockwell Automation FactoryTalk DataMosaix SaaS, AspenTech Inmation OT Data Fabric and Körber Werum PAS-X MES as distinct manufacturing integration targets with documented reusable read paths and customer-value mappings. Evidence remains specification/public-documentation level only: no sandbox or customer tenant credentials were used and all writes/control operations remain disabled.

systems.name: Rockwell Automation FactoryTalk DataMosaix / DataMosaix SaaS
systems.evidenceNote: Rockwell Automation documents REST APIs, Machine-to-Machine identities, OpenAPI specifications, access tokens, Swagger UI and API versioning for FactoryTalk DataMosaix SaaS. Current 1.13 release documentation exposes assets, timeseries, timeseries datapoints, sequences, relationships, events, datasets, labels and files through its data interfaces, with important query limits and role/capability controls. Public release material also documents Fiix extraction and Cognite Flows/App Hosting integration. No DataMosaix sandbox or tenant authentication was attempted.

requiredPermissions: customer-authorised read-only M2M/application identity scoped to the approved organisation, project and datasets
read assets, timeseries, datapoints, events, datasets and related model entities only where required by WFM
customer region/cluster bound explicitly; private connectivity used where the customer requires it
custom least-privilege role preferred over broad default Application/Extractor roles
no extractor/application/project configuration, SAP writeback, workflow execution, agent action or other mutative capability during discovery
dataAvailableOrExpected: industrial assets and their relationships
time-series definitions and timestamped datapoints
events and operational state-change context
datasets, sequences, labels and files where authorised
cross-source contextualised industrial data loaded by customer extractors/connectors
maintenance context where a customer has enabled the documented Fiix extractor
customer-defined flexible data-model entities
automationOpportunities: use machine, event and time-series state to refresh labour demand and redeployment recommendations
correlate staffing with production state, downtime and throughput without adding another direct OT tap
combine maintenance signals from customer-enabled sources such as Fiix with staffing and skill availability
reuse DataMosaix as a governed industrial aggregation layer across plants instead of duplicating source-by-source extraction
detect API/model/schema/capability changes and degrade evidence before a drifted field silently affects WFM decisions
consider any writeback, workflow or agent action only after a separately authorised sandbox write/read-back proof
customerValue: better forecasting from contextualised production signals
savingsHypotheses: reduce duplicate OT integration engineering by consuming a customer-governed industrial data layer
reduce paid idle labour by detecting verified stoppages and recovery signals earlier
reduce understaffing or overstaffing by aligning labour demand to actual production state
reduce maintenance-response delay where maintenance and machine-state context is already aggregated
reduce manual cross-site reporting by standardising asset/event/time-series inputs into WFM canonical objects
dataGaps: worker, contract, payroll and authoritative roster data are not native industrial-data objects and normally remain in HCM/WFM/payroll systems
asset names, external IDs, flexible models and event semantics are customer-specific and require explicit canonical mapping
current documentation notes that mixed FactoryTalk Optix events can include state changes, acknowledgements, confirmations and alarms without a reliable alarm-only discriminator
API/capability availability varies by release, role and customer configuration
DataMosaix data can describe production state but does not by itself prove which worker was present or qualified
constraintsRisks: regional clusters and data-residency choices must be bound per tenant and never silently cross-routed
M2M roles/capabilities are not intrinsically read-only; exact permitted operations must be verified before tenant evidence is promoted
time-series datapoint queries require bounded identifiers/time windows and large fetches can timeout or fail; current documentation reports an error above one million returned rows
API versions and the move from older asset-model APIs toward the Data Model Framework require compatibility detection and schema fingerprints
events, datasets and joins can be high volume, duplicated or late; source IDs, event time and deterministic checkpoints must be preserved
extractor/application management APIs and workflow/writeback capabilities are mutative and remain outside the read connector
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Reuse the existing REST/OpenAPI profile for a thin DataMosaix adapter. Add API/capability version discovery, explicit region/cluster binding, M2M token/claim inspection without logging tokens, bounded time-window and identifier-based timeseries pagination, deterministic source-ID dedupe, event-time versus ingestion-time handling, flexible-model schema fingerprints and customer asset/site mappings. Then obtain an authorised DataMosaix sandbox/project for least-privilege authentication and a read round-trip before considering any workflow, agent or writeback route.

systems.name: AspenTech Inmation OT Data Fabric
systems.evidenceNote: AspenTech documents Inmation as an industrial data fabric spanning cloud, edge and on-premises estates with OPC/OPC UA, ODBC, files, MQTT, Kafka, HTTP, Modbus and other OT/IT connectivity plus store-and-forward buffering for intermittent networks. Its Web API documentation exposes controlled read endpoints for current values, quality/timestamps, model hierarchy, files and historical data. Authentication supports Profile Credentials or Windows accounts with Basic or bearer-token modes. Endpoint permissions explicitly separate READ/LIST from WRITE/MODIFY and executable-function surfaces. No Inmation sandbox or tenant authentication was attempted.

requiredPermissions: dedicated customer-authorised profile limited to READ and only the minimum LIST access required for model/path discovery
site/model scope restricted to approved industrial objects and histories
read current values, quality, timestamps, hierarchy and historical data only where required
customer-edge termination for OPC UA, MQTT, Modbus and other plant-network protocols
explicit denial of WRITE, MODIFY, upload, batch-update, execfunction and process/control operations
dataAvailableOrExpected: current industrial values with source quality and timestamps
hierarchical asset/model and connector/core/parent/system paths
raw and processed historical telemetry
industrial events/signals exposed through the customer model
files and metadata stored in authorised file stores
batch production records where a customer model exposes the documented read surface
context from legacy and modern upstream sources including OPC, PI/PHD, MQTT, Kafka, ODBC and files
automationOpportunities: use current and historical machine/production state to refresh staffing requirements and downtime redeployment recommendations
coordinate maintenance windows and skill demand from industrial state without direct cloud scanning of plant networks
reuse an existing customer OT data fabric to connect legacy plants and reduce separate point-to-point OT integrations
preserve source quality and event time so low-quality or delayed telemetry cannot silently drive live staffing automation
resume buffered site ingestion after outages using per-site watermarks and deterministic dedupe
correlate cross-site production and labour outcomes for forecasting and executive reporting
savingsHypotheses: reduce connector engineering by reusing the customer's governed industrial data fabric
reduce paid idle labour through earlier trustworthy downtime/recovery signals
reduce emergency maintenance overtime through better operational-state coordination
reduce data-loss reconciliation effort at intermittently connected sites through store-and-forward aware ingestion
reduce manual cross-system reporting by retaining source lineage and canonical industrial mappings
dataGaps: industrial namespaces, paths, tags, files and model semantics are customer-specific
workforce identity, payroll, absence and authoritative roster data usually remain outside the OT data fabric
legacy source quality and timestamps can vary materially across connected systems
a secure tunnel or aggregated fabric does not prove that each upstream tag is semantically suitable for a WFM decision
exact availability of batch, event and model content depends on customer configuration and connected sources
constraintsRisks: store-and-forward can replay old data after connectivity returns; delayed telemetry must never be mistaken for current machine state
Basic or Windows-integrated authentication requires deployment-specific hardening; bearer/profile credentials are preferred when they can be scoped safely
large historical reads require bounded time windows, checkpoints and backpressure
duplicate observations can enter through multiple upstream collectors and must be deduplicated with source lineage intact
the Web API exposes WRITE, MODIFY and executable-function capabilities; the WFM credential must be technically prevented from reaching them
edge and plant protocols require a customer-controlled gateway and no direct cloud plant-network access
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Reuse the existing REST, OPC UA, MQTT, Kafka, database, file and Modbus profiles rather than building new transports. Add a thin Inmation Web API adapter that discovers only authorised model paths, enforces READ/LIST-only operation allowlists, preserves value/quality/source timestamp, reads bounded history, tracks per-site watermarks, deduplicates buffered replay, fingerprints customer model mappings and records source lineage. Keep all plant protocols at the customer edge and prohibit WRITE/MODIFY/execfunction routes. Then obtain an authorised test profile for sandbox/tenant authentication and a read round-trip.

systems.name: Körber Werum PAS-X MES
systems.evidenceNote: Körber documents Werum PAS-X MES interfaces using industrial standards including OPC, XML and REST and integration with ERP, DCS/SCADA/Historians, LIMS/ELN and DMS under ISA-95/ISA-88 functional models. Public PAS-X material describes scheduling, equipment management/status, performance/OEE and downtime, material/warehouse flow, electronic batch records and track-and-trace. The exact customer interface package, authentication and licensed modules vary by deployment; therefore only the evidenced REST plus vendor-thin industrial-integration path is catalogued and no tenant authentication was attempted.

requiredPermissions: customer-authorised read-only MES integration/service identity scoped to the approved site and production areas
read production/order/batch status, equipment state, schedule and performance data only where the customer's licensed interface exposes it
read material/warehouse and quality/process context only when required for a defined WFM workflow
no master-batch-record design, electronic-signature, approval, batch-release, user-rights, equipment-control or process-control permission
validated customer change-control approval before connecting to a regulated production environment
dataAvailableOrExpected: production and batch/order execution state
planned and as-is production scheduling context
equipment status, cleaning state, counters and timers where enabled
performance/OEE and downtime context
material flow, warehouse and inventory context
process and quality results captured by the MES
electronic batch-record/report metadata and track-and-trace context where licensed
standard interface messages to ERP, automation, laboratory and document systems
automationOpportunities: refresh staffing demand from actual batch/order progress instead of static production plans
coordinate labour redeployment around verified equipment downtime, cleaning and recovery states
align maintenance and specialist skill demand to equipment state and planned production windows
use material-flow constraints to avoid staffing a line that cannot run and to redirect labour to executable work
correlate OEE, downtime and labour outcomes for shift learning and executive reporting
reuse the customer's PAS-X standard interfaces and integration content rather than duplicating validated point-to-point logic
savingsHypotheses: reduce paid idle time by aligning staffing with actual executable batch/equipment state
reduce overtime and disruption cost by coordinating specialist labour with downtime, cleaning and maintenance windows
reduce manual shift/production reconciliation by consuming MES execution and OEE evidence
reduce avoidable staffing against material-constrained production
reduce validated integration effort by reusing PAS-X standard interfaces and customer-approved message contracts
dataGaps: the exact interface APIs/messages, authentication method and licensed modules are customer/version specific and need contract discovery
MES user tracking or electronic-signature identity is not an authoritative HR roster, pay rule or absence source
skills/qualification truth may live in LMS/QMS/HCM even when PAS-X enforces production rights
customer-specific MBRs, content and equipment models can materially change data semantics
not every PAS-X deployment exposes all equipment, OEE, warehouse, quality or track-and-trace modules
constraintsRisks: cloud, private-cloud and on-premises deployments can expose different network and integration arrangements
validated GMP environments require formal customer change control, traceability and carefully bounded read access
multiple PAS-X versions and customer content require interface/version fingerprints and regression fixtures
the same order, equipment or material can appear in ERP, MES and automation sources; deterministic source priority and duplicate reconciliation are required
industrial integration can be bidirectional or process-controlling; no MES/equipment/process write is allowed through the WFM read connector
regulated batch and identity records require minimisation and retention controls
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Reuse the existing REST and vendor-thin industrial-integration profiles. Implement a thin PAS-X adapter contract around customer-approved interface definitions with deployment/version/module discovery, read-only operation allowlists, ISA-95-style order/batch/work-centre/equipment canonical mappings, deterministic ERP-MES duplicate reconciliation, schema/version fingerprints and validated-environment diagnostics. Treat MSI/equipment/process control, batch release, electronic signature and other writes as separately prohibited capabilities until an authorised sandbox write-roundtrip and customer safety/quality approval exist.
